task: M4 part 1: priority-stack QoS (RELIABLE+deadline+MANUAL_BY_TOPIC liveliness+transport_priority) on PropulsionState toggled by ENABLE_PRIORITY_QOS, sensor_burst.idl + load-generator flood, propulsion-monitor latency recorder, tools/run_scenario_congestion.sh 3-phase A/B, tools/compare_congestion_phases.py verdict logic
route: single model, primary session (Claude Sonnet 5), no crosscheck call — executing ADR-0006's already-scoped 2-of-4-layers decision, not an architecture debate
notes: Two real bugs caught by actually building/running, not by inspection: (1) middleware/dds/dds_entity.hpp's Entity wrapper (dds_entity_t/int32) was used to hold a dds_qos_t* pointer -- a real type-safety bug the compiler caught immediately, fixed by adding a separate Qos RAII class; (2) dds_get_deadline_missed_status doesn't exist -- the reader-side API is dds_get_requested_deadline_missed_status, also caught by the build. First congestion-scenario attempt (10Hz signal, 500Hz/2KB flood, 30s phases, n~98-296) came back genuinely INCONCLUSIVE -- the verdict logic correctly identified the flood wasn't stressful enough rather than reporting a misleading pass/fail on noise. Re-ran with 50Hz signal + 3000Hz/4KB flood (n~1400): PASS, p99 454.8us (priority) vs 839.9us (no-priority) under the identical flood, vs 498.1us unloaded baseline. Far-tail (p99.9/max) got WORSE under priority QoS (likely RELIABLE-QoS retransmission stalls) -- disclosed as a caveat in the report, not hidden, since claiming priority QoS improves every percentile would be an unsupported claim.

notes: Two more real bugs caught by running the scenario end-to-end, not by inspection: (1) `docker compose down` (no --profile flag) silently leaves profile-gated services (load-generator, propulsion-monitor) running -- fixed the congestion script's cleanup to pass --profile congestion to down too, not just up; (2) central's base docker-compose.yml service never actually referenced RECORD_PATH/RECORD_DURATION_S via interpolation, so setting them as shell env vars silently did nothing outside the M1 benchmark overlay -- fixed by adding the interpolated keys directly to central's base definition. Once fixed: injected 300ms tc netem delay on rear-zone produced a measured latency jump from 134us mean to 304,682us (within 0.1% of injected value) and recovered to 123us within 2s of clearing the fault -- an unusually clean, convincing result from real network-level fault injection.

task: M5: telemetry-bridge (C++, DDS subscriber, atomic JSON snapshot) + api-bridge (Python/FastAPI, REST+WebSocket+OpenAPI on :8282, UDS-inspired diagnostics, docker-socket-mounted fault-control endpoints), tools/mostrider_cli.py, docs/architecture/security-limitations.md, services/diagnostics executive summary
route: single model, primary session (Claude Sonnet 5), no crosscheck call -- a platform-compatibility spike changed the plan mid-flight (see ADR-0007), not an architecture debate over uncertain requirements
notes: Real, confirmed platform gap found by spiking before building: the official cyclonedds PyPI package (11.0.1) has no linux/arm64 wheel -- pip install fails at metadata-generation even with CYCLONEDDS_HOME/CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH/--no-build-isolation set correctly against the apt-installed C library. Split the bridge in two (C++ DDS participant + Python file/subprocess consumer) rather than force x86_64 emulation. Three more real bugs caught by running the full stack, not by inspection: (1) docker.io + docker-compose-v2 install cleanly from Ubuntu 24.04's default apt repos -- confirmed before committing to the design, not assumed; (2) api-bridge's docker-compose calls initially failed with 'mounts denied: path not shared from host' -- a classic Docker-outside-of-Docker pitfall where relative bind-mount paths resolved against the container's own filesystem view (/workspace) instead of the real host path the daemon needs; fixed with explicit -f (container-visible compose file path) plus --project-directory (host path, via ${PWD} interpolation) kept deliberately separate; (3) the first fix attempt broke compose file discovery entirely ('no configuration file provided') because --project-directory also changes where compose looks for the file by default -- required both flags together, not just one. Verified end-to-end: CLI stop-zone -> REST -> docker compose stop -> central's discovery module -> telemetry-bridge snapshot -> API reflects zone alive=false, full round trip confirmed live. WebSocket handshake confirmed via raw HTTP Upgrade headers (101 Switching Protocols) since no local websockets client was available.  10 OpenAPI paths auto-documented at /docs.

route: single model, primary session (Claude Sonnet 5), no crosscheck call -- executing the named M6 dashboard deliverable, refining the panel-proposed chart-library choice against the dataviz skill's own method rather than debating it
notes: Followed CLAUDE.md's UI-testing rule literally: installed Playwright + Chromium and screenshotted the running app in both themes before calling this done, rather than asserting it worked from reading the code. That caught two real bugs no amount of code review would have: (1) uPlot resolves CSS custom properties to colors once at chart-creation time (canvas strokeStyle doesn't track CSS var changes) -- the light-theme screenshot showed the chart still using dark-mode's --gridline value, fixed by keying the chart's creation effect on the theme prop; (2) ZoneCards' 'Xs ago' label was actively misleading -- TopologyState only republishes on alive/stale transitions, not every heartbeat, so a zone alive for 40+ minutes correctly showed a large 'ago' number that reads as a false staleness warning; relabeled to 'alive for Xm Ys'. Also caught and fixed a local-dev-vs-Docker path mismatch before it broke anything: the tokens.css import path assumed the full repo tree, which doesn't exist inside the Docker build stage unless the same relative directory layout is preserved -- fixed via predev/prebuild npm scripts plus a matching-layout Dockerfile stage rather than two diverging import paths. Verified live end-to-end via a real browser click (not curl): Stop button -> REST -> docker compose stop -> central's discovery module -> snapshot -> WebSocket -> UI shows the zone stale within seconds, with a new diagnostic warning appearing in the log. Zero browser console errors across all screenshots.
